thread:
maria: Kicking off SwapDay POC thread — client wants a drop-in replacement for CompetitorX. Main asks: prompt parity, response deltas, pricing impact, and security questionnaire. Can SEs confirm what we need to validate first?
ajay: Quick wins: endpoint mapping + token counting. We should capture a set of 50 representative prompts and compare outputs.
sam: For mapping, note CompetitorX uses `X-Trace-Id` and our API expects `x-request-id`. We'll need a small header shim. Example shim: 
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -H 'X-Trace-Id: 123' https://api.competitorx.ai/generate \\n  -> translate to -> https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete with header x-request-id:123
```
ajay: Also need to call out streaming differences: CompetitorX streams in SSE chunks with event:token, we stream chunked JSON lines. That will affect UX and error retry. Recommend adding a client-side compatibility handler.
maria: Price question from the AE: client does 2M tokens/month today. What's the likely delta if they switch to us with our batching and KV cache?
ben: With our batching + prefix caching I'd expect token cost to drop ~15-25% for typical convo flows, but depends on prompt length and repetition. If they use stateful sessions (long history) they'd benefit more. Need to run their sample traces.
nina: Security blockers — they require SAML SSO, IP allowlist, and proof of KMS integrations for encryption at rest. Can we answer the standard Enterprise questionnaire items on KMS key rotation and no-key-escrow?
sam: For KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private + Dedicated. For Hosted API we offer envelope encryption and have SOC2 status — I'll attach the short blurb.
deploy-bot: New POC ticket created: SWAPDAY-1243 — assigned to @ajay and @ben — due 2024-06-05
ajay: We should prepare three artifacts for the client POC: 1) adapter shim (header + streaming compatibility), 2) prompt mapping doc (with sample input/expected output diffs), 3) cost model spreadsheet showing token accounting delta.
maria: Can we get an ETA for the adapter shim? Client wants to start integration this week.
ajay: I can produce a reference shim by EOD tomorrow. It'll be a tiny node proxy they can run in their infra.
ben: I'll run token accounting with their 2M monthly trace once they share logs — pinged them for uploads.
nina: I'll start filling security questionnaire answers. One note: they asked for Azure VNet peering — that's a Dedicated/private-only ask. Flagging for legal/ops.
maria: Legal will need to review VNet peering ask. Also client asked about licensing model for committed throughput vs pay-as-you-go. Any presales calc?
\en: (typo)
ben: Licensing: Hosted: usage-based; Dedicated: committed monthly capacity + overage. I can draft a sample commit that matches their current spend — will post numbers after I run the trace.
ajay: On prompt parity: sometimes we see subtle tokenization differences -> result wording shifts. For demo, we'll create a matched-eval harness and surface delta examples (e.g., hallucination, length, stop-token behavior). Small example diff: 
```
Prompt: "Summarize the org chart"
CompetitorX: "Alice (CEO), Bob (CTO),..."
Redwood(with mapping): "Alice — CEO
Bob — CTO
"
```
maria: Good. Action items: @ajay build shim + sample harness; @ben run token delta and price model; @nina draft security answers and flag infra asks to legal. I'll compile and send the Q/A packet to the client Friday.
ajay: Got it. Will also add a short README: `how to swap endpoints` and a troubleshooting checklist (CORS, stream differences, retry semantics).
ben: FYI: if the client uses stateful sessions and wants sticky KV, recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput. I'll note latency SLAs.
nina: One more security note: client requires TLS 1.3 minimum and mutual TLS for internal services — we support mTLS on Dedicated. Flagging as an enterprise blocker for Hosted.
maria: Thanks team. I'll follow up after the client uploads logs. :thumbsup:
